JUDGMENT 1.

Vide this common judgment, I shall decide the instant two DAR matters filed separately by the Investigating Agency in respect of death of Sh. Desh Pal Singh (hereinafter, the 'deceased') in MACT no.176/2020 as well as the injuries sustained by Sh. Aman (hereinafter, the 'injured') in MACT no.
177/2020, in the same motor vehicular accident which occurred on 13.03.2020 at 11:55 p.m. at Red Light, Durga Puri Chowk, Delhi.
2. In connection with the accident, FIR no.107/2020, under sections 279/337/304-A IPC was registered at PS Jyoti Nagar, Delhi on the statement of injured Aman.

As per FIR, on the aforesaid d a t e ,
 
t i m e ______________________________________________________________________ and place, the injured/ petitioner Aman, aged 22 years, was going from Shahdara to Loni Gol Chakkar on the motorcycle bearing number UP81BQ-6329.
One person wearing Khaki uniform (the deceased Desh Pal Singh) standing at roadside took lift on the said motorcycle.

On reaching at Durga Puri Chowk Red Light, finding the signal as green, while they were crossing the signal, at the same time, a Tata-407 vehicle bearing number UP23T-5782 (hereinafter, "offending vehicle"), being driven by its driver at a high speed, rashly, negligently, came from Babarpur side and hit the motorcycle with a violent force.
As a result of the accident, along with the motorcycle, the motorcylist Aman fell on the road and received injuries.
The pillion rider Desh Pal Singh also fell down on road and his head was crushed under the right side rear tyre of the offending vehicle.
The driver of the offending vehicle fled away leaving the offending vehicle at the spot.
Both the injured were removed to GTB Hospital, where injured Desh Pal Singh was declared brought dead vide MLC no. BD-797/03/2020 and injured Aman was medically examined vide MLC no.C-2261/25/2020.

3. During investigation, it was found out that at the time of accident, the offending vehicle was being driven and owned by the respondent no.1 and was insured with respondent no.2/ insurance company.

After completion of the investigation, the charge-sheet was filed against the respondent no.1 in the concerned court and the present DARs were filed before this Tribunal, which have been treated as claim petitions under Section 166 of the 'Motor Vehicle Act, 1988' on behalf of the c l a i m a n t (

5. Respondent no.2/ insurer in its written-statement admitted that the alleged offending vehicle bearing registration number UP23T-5722 was insurerd with it vide Policy no. 0160379584 for the period from 27.09.2019 to 26.09.2020 in the name of Rifakat Ali.

However, it inter-alia stated that as per DAR, the offending vehicle was registered in Amroha, whereas, the accident took place in Delhi and the Permit of the vehicle has not been filed alongwith the DAR, which shows that the vehicle was being driven without valid Permit in violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy and as such, the answering respondent cannot be held liable for paying compensation to the petitioners.

UP23T-5782 being driven by respondent no.1/ driver?

On the other hand, insurance company got issued summons to call Record Clerk from RTO, Amroha, U.P., who did not appear despite service and therefore, notice under Order 16 rule 12 CPC, followed by Bailable Warrants were issued against the witness.

However, vide order dated 15.04.2025, this Tribunal observed that the Permit of the offending vehicle is also part of the DAR, which specifically mentions "regions for which Permit is valid: All U.P." and since the documents were collected by the IO during investigation, there is no reason to dispute the authenticity of the Permit collected by the IO and therefore, this Tribunal dispensed with the evidence of insurance company and since learned counsel for the insurance company submitted that no other evidence is to be led, respondents' evidence was closed.
10.
This Tribunal heard the final arguments advanced by learned counsels for the parties and also perused the evidence and other materials placed on record.

The findings of the Tribunal on the issues are as under:-
ISSUE NO.1 (in both cases)
11. Issue no.1, being interlinked in both the cases, shall be decided here together by a common finding.
For deciding the issue in hand, the deposition of PW3 Aman, who received injuries in the accident, is relevant to be appreciated.
12. PW3 Aman @ Aman Shekhawat deposed on the lines of the FIR which was registered on his statement.
PW3 Aman stated that on 13.03.2020, he was travelling on motorcycle bearing number UP81BQ6329 from Shahdara to Loni Gol Chakkar.
One Mr. Desh Pal Singh, who was standing on the road, which goes from Shahdara to Durgapuri, signalled him to stop as he wanted lift.

PW3 Aman further stated that he slowed down his motorcycle and made him sit as pillion rider and when they reached Durgapuri Red Light, at around 11:55 p.m., the offending vehicle bearing no.
UP23T-5782 being driven at a high speed, rashly and negligently, came from Babarpur side and hit their motorcycle.
PW3 stated that due to the impact of said accident, he and Desh Pal Singh fell down from the motorcycle and suffered injuries.
The right side tyre of the offending vehicle crushed the head of Desh Pal Singh, who died on the spot.
PW3 Aman stated that he and Desh Pal Singh were taken to GTB Hospital for treatment, where Desh Pal Singh was declared brought dead and he was given treatment of injuries sustained by him.
PW3 Aman stated that in connection with the accident, he got lodged the FIR no.107/20, under sections 279/338/304-A IPC, PS Jyoti Nagar.
13. The eye-witness PW3 Aman was cross
-examined at length by learned counsel for the insurance company.

On perusal of the entire cross-examination of PW3 Aman, this Tribunal finds nothing Dar-Aman vs Rifakat Ali on 3 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84408929/
5 which may demolish or discredit his testimony on the aspect of rash and negligent act of respondent no.1 while driving the offending vehicle.
Besides, nothing else is available on record which may s u g g e s t a n y f a l s i t y o r u n t r u t h i n t h e o r a l t e s t i m o n y o f t h i s e y e - w i t n e s s .

14. In the facts and circumstances of the present case, the rashness and negligence of the respondent no.1 in driving the offending vehicle was that the respondent no.1 had jumped the red light, which was the precipitating factor leading to the accident, as from the side from where PW3 Aman was coming it was green light for him.
To the specific query put by the Tribunal to PW3 Aman if Tata-407 jumped the red light, he replied that, "Yes, Tata-407 had jumped the red light and also it was being driven at a high-speed."

The said fact is uncontested, as no one on behalf of the driver of the offending vehicle/ respondent no.1 has cross-examined PW3 Aman on this aspect and the said statement of fact in the deposition has to be taken by the Tribunal as the best approximation to the truth of the facts of the case of the petitioner.
Jumping red light by any vehicle without any explanation for it is prima facie a rash and negligent act.
If it is a red light for a particular side of the road, it would be the green light for the other road users.

15. Also, the deposition of the eye-witness PW3 Aman qua involvement of the offending vehicle and occurrence of the accident due to rash/ negligent driving of the respondent no.1, is found corroborated from the DAR comprising of FIR, Site Plan, Seizure Memo as well as mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle and that of the motorcycle of victim, MLC of the injured and MLC as well as postmortem report of the deceased and chargesheet, etc.
16.

It is evident that FIR was registered in the matter on the same day of accident and description a n d r e g i s t r a t i o n n u m b e r o f t h e o f f e n d i n g ______________________________________________________________________ vehicle is found clearly mentioned in the FIR.
The seizure memo of the offending vehicle and that of the motorcycle of the victim shows that the same were taken into police possession from the spot of accident itself in the accidental conditions.
17. Moreover, there is no challenge from the respondent no.1/ driver of the offending vehicle to the version of the eye-witness.

The respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of the eye-witness regarding the above accident and its manner but he preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.

Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009(3) AD (Delhi)
310.
18.

A perusal of the MLC no.B/797/03/2020 of the deceased Desh Pal Singh, which is part of the DAR makes it clear that he was brought to GTB Hospital with the history of RTA (Road Traffic A c c i d e n t )
 
a t ______________________________________________________________________ Durgapuri Chowk at around 12:07 a.m. on 14.03.2020 as stated by brought by and was declared,
'brought dead'.

Further, the postmortem conducted at UCMS & GTB Hospital, Delhi vide postmortem report no. 449/2020, multiple antemortem injuries were observed and cause of death was opined to be shock as a result of antemortem injury to head produced by blunt force impact.
20.

And MLC no.C/2261/25/2020 of the injured Aman, which is part of the DAR, shows that he was brought to GTB Hospital with the history of RTA at Durgapuri Chowk at around 11:30 p.m. on 13.03.2020 as stated by himself and injuries suffered by him were opined to be 'simple' in nature.

The fact that Aman had also received injuries in the accident in conjugation with the fact that the PW3 Rajendra Prasad, the Investigating Officer has deposed to in his deposition that he had prepared complete DAR at the instance of Aman and had also filed the same lends additional credence to the case of the petitioners.

21. Also, it is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability,
the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
______________________________________________________________________ Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &
Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.

ISSUE NO. 2 (In both cases)

In view of common finding on issue no.1, petitioners in both the cases are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittances.

In view of the aforesaid judgments, the compensation in the present case has to be ascertained as under:
PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age of deceased & Application of Multiplier 25.

The copy of Election I.D. Card of the deceased, which is at page no.59 of the DAR, shows the date of birth of the deceased as 10.07.1965, which would mean that on the date of the accident (13.03.2020), the deceased was 54 years of age.

Accordingly, the multiplier of 11 shall be applicable,
as the deceased belonged to the age group 51-55 years (refer: Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.
Assessment of Income of deceased 26.

PW1 Rambiri, wife of the deceased has deposed that the deceased Desh Pal Singh was working as Bus Marshal in Delhi Home Guards, Directorate General of Home Guards, Govt of NCT of Delhi and was drawing a salary of Rs.22,671/- per month.

28.

Accordingly,
income of deceased is assessed Rs.22,733/- per month.

Future Prospects 29.
The deceased, who was aged 54 years of age at the time of the accident, was receiving a fixed salary.

Belonging to age group 50 to 60 years, an addition of 10% to the income of the deceased has to be considered towards future prospects [(refer: Pranay Sethi (Supra)].
Deduction Towards Personal Living Expenses 30.
PW1 Rambiri, wife of the deceased has deposed that the deceased has left behind a family of four members consisting of his wife and three children, who all were entirely dependent upon the deceased.
As per copy of Aadhaar Cards of the children, which are part of the ______________________________________________________________________

DAR, it reveals that at the time of accident, the elder son namely Pratap Singh was 24 years old,
unmarried daughter Geeta was aged 27 years old and younger son Ravi Kumar was aged 19 years.

In her cross-examination conducted through Ld. Court Commissioner, PW1 Rambiri categorically denied the suggestion that she and her children were not dependent upon the deceased and stated that she is not getting any pension and that no one from her family has got compassionate appointment.

Therefore, considering the four claimants herein as dependent upon the deceased,
one-fourth of the income of deceased has to be deducted towards his personal living expenses [(refer: as Reshma Kumari & Ors. v. Madan Mohan & Anr., (2013) 9 SCC 65].

during his evidence has relied upon only two documents i.e. his Aadhaar Card as Ex.PW1/1 and DAR as Ex.PW1/2 (dated 02.05.2024).
35. The only document with respect to the treatment or medical examination of the petitioner is the MLC no. C/2261/25/2020, dated 14.03.2020, which is part of the DAR (Ex.PW1/2).

Perusal of this document shows that on medical examination, the petitioner was observed to have suffered abrasion over right hand wrist and he made complaints of having pain in left knee and right thigh.
Further, the MLC makes it clear that the injury received by the petitioner has been opined to be "simple" in nature.
Except this MLC, there is no other document on record to show any further visit to hospital or any medical expenses incurred on treatment.

36. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that interest of justice would be served if the petitioner Aman is awarded a lump sum compensation of Rs.10,000/-
for pain and sufferings/ mental and physical shock.
Accordingly, the petitioner in this case is entitled to a compensation of Rs.10,000/-.

10 ______________________________________________________________________ LIABILITY 38.

Learned counsel for the insurance company has argued that as per Permit of the offending vehicle, it was permitted to be driven only in U.P. and not in Delhi, whereas, the accident had taken place in Delhi, which is the violation of the condition of the insurance policy and therefore, the insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation.

Learned counsel further submitted that in order to prove that the Permit was valid for U.P. only, he made efforts to summon the Record Clerk from RTO, Amroha, U.P., who did not appear despite service and this Tribunal vide order dated 15.04.2025 dispensed with the evidence of respondent/ insurance company on the said point.

39. Vide order dated 15.04.2025, this Tribunal has observed that:
"Perusal of record reveals that permit no.
UP-21/112/GOOD/2016/20264 of the offending vehicle bearing registration number UP23T-5782 is also part of the DAR, which specifically mentions "regions for which Permit is valid 3: All U.P."
There is no reason to dispute the authenticity of the documents/ permit collected by the IO.
Therefore, the Tribunal dispenss with the evidence of respondent/ insurance company on the said point."
40. I have perused the copy of insurance policy and copy of Permit of offending vehicle, which are part of the DAR.

The insurance policy contains "Limitation as to Use" clause, which specifies the use of insured vehicle only under the Permit; however, as per the Permit, the area for which Permit was valid is mentioned as "All U.P."

Thus, it stands established on record that there was a clear violation o f  
t h e ______________________________________________________________________ "Limitation as to Use" clause of the insurance policy.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Jumping red light by any vehicle without any explanation for it is prima facie a rash and negligent act.
If it is a red light for a particular side of the road, it would be the green light for the other road users.
It is evident that FIR was registered in the matter on the same day of accident and description a n d r e g i s t r a t i o n n u m b e r o f t h e o f f e n d i n g ______________________________________________________________________ vehicle is found clearly mentioned in the FIR.
The seizure memo of the offending vehicle and that of the motorcycle of the victim shows that the same were taken into police possession from the spot of accident itself in the accidental conditions.
The respondent no.1 was the best witness, who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the testimony of the eye-witness regarding the above accident and its manner but he preferred not to enter into the witness box during the course of inquiry.
Thus, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against him to the effect that the accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by him in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Kamlesh, 2009(3) AD (Delhi)
310.
18.
Not only this, the respondent no.1 was charge-sheeted in the criminal case by the police after detailed investigation and in a motor vehicle accident claim case, the contents of chargesheet are admissible in evidence and deemed to be correct under Rule 7 of Delhi Motor Accident Tribunal Rules, 2008, which support the version of eye- witness regarding rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1.
21. Also, it is settled proposition of law that in an action founded on the principle of fault liability,
the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine-qua-non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
In the light of the above discussion and the evidence brought on record, it is held that the petitioner(s) have been able to prove on the basis of the preponderance of probabilities that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into death of deceased Desh Pal Singh and injuries to the petitioner Aman.
In view of common finding on issue no.1, petitioners in both the cases are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittances.
